newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes flat with WTI, ample supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes flat with WTI, ample supply.

text.p: Prices for U.S. West Coast light crudes were flat Monday, holding at Friday's February spot market levels for West Texas Intermediate (WTI) amid thin trade, traders said.
With no new Alaska North Slope deals reported Monday and diffs flat at $1.45 under March WTI, outright ANS prices were unchanged at $22.30/22.50 a barrel.
BP America, a key producer, was asking for $1.25 below March NYMEX, with bidders were as wide as $1.50 a barrel under.
Meanwhile, trader remained static trade for Alaskan crude, traders said.
Heavy California grades were also flat despite turnarounds at plants operated by Mobil, Tosco, and Chevron.
The outages kept extra crude in storage and forced companies to cut published prices late last week.
Traders also said weak WTI prices and additional crude left by last week's fire at Tosco Avon weighed on the market.
One trader heard the fire may have forced Tosco to cancel February heavy crude purchases from a large independent seller in California.
California oil companies offered heavy oil for 25 cents a barrel less than early last week, and traders reported cargoes sold at 50 to 25 cents under those averages.
Outright prices for Kern River, a representative heavy grade, were offered at $18.25 and bid about $18 Monday.
Wilmington, a heavy grade produced in Long Beach, Calif., was sold in the range of 70 to 80 cents over posted averages, representing a rise from recent weeks amid natural production declines.
